title: SF security deposit interest
rule: San Francisco landlords must pay tenants simple (not compounded) interest on security deposits every year on the annual due date (the day and month the landlord received the deposit), at the Rent Board rate in effect when the payment is due. No interest is due if the tenant leaves before one full year. It applies to all SF residential rental units, including those exempt from the Rent Ordinance, but not to government-assisted or subsidized units. Interest can be paid directly or as a rent credit. For units covered by the Rent Ordinance, the landlord may deduct 50% of the annual Rent Board fee from each year's interest. When a tenant moves out, interest owed is due within two weeks.

params.rate_applied: rate in effect when the payment is due (annual due date)
params.fee_share_note: Landlord may deduct 50% of the annual Rent Board fee from each year of interest, only for units covered by the Rent Ordinance. Amounts after 2024-2025 not verified.

verify_phrase: rate in effect when the security deposit interest payment is due
